items.headline: Claude's phone app gets a fresh new look, starting on iPhone
items.summary: Anthropic began gradually rolling out a redesigned Claude mobile app on November 20, starting with iOS. Your chats, projects, and plan stay exactly the same, and there's nothing to switch on, but the new look needs iOS 26 or later.
items.why_it_matters: If you use Claude on your phone and it suddenly looks different, nothing is broken or lost; just keep the app and your iPhone updated to get it.

items.headline: ChatGPT had a major outage Friday, with up to 75% of requests failing
items.summary: OpenAI's own status page says a large share of ChatGPT and OpenAI requests failed between 1:48 and 5:21 PT on November 21, peaking at a 75% failure rate for both free and paid users. OpenAI has published a write-up of the incident.
items.why_it_matters: If your business leans on one AI tool for daily work, a few hours of downtime can stall you, so it's worth having a second assistant (like Claude or Gemini) set up and ready.

categories.title: Tools & Tips for Creators and Small Biz

items.headline: HighLevel tests a free tool that shows whether AI chatbots mention your business
items.summary: HighLevel (GoHighLevel), a marketing platform many small agencies use, opened a private beta of 'AI & Search Visibility.' It checks your website for SEO problems and tracks whether your business shows up in answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode.
items.why_it_matters: More customers now ask an AI chatbot for recommendations instead of searching Google, so a tool that shows whether those bots know about you is a practical first step, if you're already a HighLevel user and get beta access.

items.headline: YouTube shows off a new lineup of creator-made shows and films
items.summary: At its second Creator Premieres event in Los Angeles, YouTube announced a slate of recurring shows, documentaries, and interactive series from creators like Emma Chamberlain and Nick DiGiovanni, running through 2026 and 2027. Phil Rosenthal is even moving the new season of Somebody Feed Phil from Netflix to his own YouTube channel.
items.why_it_matters: YouTube is betting that longer, TV-style series from creators are the future of the platform, a signal that a recurring show format on your channel lines up with where YouTube is pushing.
